posture_bench.name: Posture Bench
posture_bench.description: Four artifacts declare an axis called posture and no two of them share a value list - fifteen words, one overlap, the least agreed axis left in the corpus. This bench puts ten of those words on ONE articulated body: a mount and a chain of six equal links on six hinges bending in one vertical plane, where a posture IS six numbers and nothing else. The brief said the four vocabularies are four kinds of thing - a defence STATE, a mechanical LOAD, an animal STANCE, a text LAYOUT. The code says three: armadillo_eggling's ball/walker are the two ENDPOINTS of _fold_amount, which armadillo_droideka._apply_fold_pose drives every hinge off linearly, and spring_hopper's drawn/laden/solid are three SAMPLES of _rest doing exactly the same job, so the state and the load are one scalar wearing two nouns. What is left is a scalar, a target point (tentacle_placer solves a chain to a Vector3) and an arrangement (qfep_formula_3d distributes N items along a path). And two of the words turn out to be one body: qfep's line is _arrange_curved at sweep 0, all hinges at zero, while tentacle_placer's sentry aims at (0, 6, 0) against a chain that is exactly 6.0 m long, so it takes the solver's own unreachable branch - comment: straighten the chain at the target - and is also all hinges at zero. A LAYOUT word and a STANCE word from two artifacts that share no vocabulary name the same six numbers to the byte. A 0.80 x 0.36 m plate carries a four-post cage 0.684 m tall, so the world box is identical in all thirty cells while the figure inside it runs from 0.145 x 0.169 m at ball to 0.000 x 0.420 m at line. Every angle is arithmetic or a bisection on a monotone function - no RandomNumberGenerator, no noise, no _process, no Timer.
dev_themes: a pose is a vector of angles
a layout is a body at constant curvature
the sentinel that is an all-rungs value in time
interactions: put line and sentry side by side in any of the three readings. They are the same photograph, and that is the point: a typographic arrangement at sweep zero and a robot arm aiming past its own reach are one pose vector, [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], arrived at from two artifacts that agree about nothing else

walk the posture axis in the joints reading and watch what each vocabulary DOES to the six wedges. armadillo alternates two big opposed angles down the chain, because a limb alternates hips and knees. spring_hopper and qfep both hand every hinge the same number. tentacle_placer bends five hinges alike and spends the sixth aiming. Three constructions, ten words

compare solid against arc in the body reading. 20.93 degrees per hinge against 18.33, and neither number was chosen: one is what a spring compressed to 0.90 leaves of its coil height under that member's own floor of 0.15, the other is 110 degrees of typographic sweep divided by six. Two derivations from two unrelated artifacts landing 2.60 degrees apart

stand at ring and look for the tip. There isn't one - at 60 degrees per hinge over six hinges the chain closes on itself and the last link ends exactly at the mount it left. Tip distance 0.000 m, the only zero in the sheet, and it is what sweep = TAU means when the thing being arranged is a body

read the envelope of ball against the envelope of line. The curl is 62 per cent LARGER, 0.0219 m2 against 0.0135, which refutes the obvious claim about defence states: a straight stick occupies almost no volume and is maximally exposed. What a curl minimises is reach, and reach is not hull
posture_bench.capacity: SEE that four artifacts can share a word and mean four different constructions by it, that two of those four constructions are the same scalar under two nouns, and that two words from two unrelated vocabularies can name the same body to the byte - and that none of this is visible from any one member, because a family's disagreement only shows up when its words are built on one object

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE CAGE IS THE FOOTPRINT AND IT IS DRAWN BEFORE EITHER AXIS IS CONSULTED: a 0.80 x 0.36 m plate 0.024 m thick, four 0.024 m posts standing 0.660 m above it at x, z = +-0.385, +-0.165, and a 0.052 m mount 0.200 m tall at the centre. The posts are the reason the AABB is a constant, and they carry more here than they did on cohort_bench because THIS FIGURE CHANGES SIZE BY A FACTOR OF THREE: the drawn body spans 0.145 x 0.169 m at ball, 0.121 x 0.140 m at ring, 0.167 x 0.188 m at coil, 0.275 x 0.277 m at laden, 0.197 x 0.356 m at walker, 0.324 x 0.183 m at arc, 0.328 x 0.157 m at solid, 0.364 x 0.169 m at cast, and 0.000 x 0.420 m at line and sentry. Measured clearances across all ten poses and all three readings: the tallest limb tops out 0.040 m below the posts, the tallest grown hull 0.025 m below them, the longest reach stops 0.021 m short of a post in x and its hull 0.006 m short, and the lowest thing any pose draws - ring, which hangs below its own hinge - sits 0.080 m above the plate. The world box is 0.80 x 0.684 x 0.36 in every one of the thirty cells. layout=ladder stands all ten postures in a row at 0.86 m pitch, about 8.5 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants; no Godot was run. The box is the STAGE and nothing else: the plate spans x at +-0.40 and z at +-0.18, and the tallest things in any cell are the four cage posts, topping out at PLATE_T + CAGE_H = 0.684. Nothing either axis draws can exceed that - every one of the ten poses was walked on the replica in all three readings and the extreme values are +0.379 m in x (cast, envelope reading, hull grown by the limb half-width), +0.659 m in y (line and sentry, envelope) and +0.104 m at the lowest point (ring, envelope), against post faces at 0.385 and 0.684 and a plate top at 0.024.

dna.default: posture=ball, reading=body. ball because IT IS THE ONLY MEMBER DEFAULT THIS BENCH CAN KEEP, and that is a counted fact rather than a preference: of the four members, armadillo_eggling ships `ball`, qfep_formula_3d ships `line`, and BOTH spring_hopper and tentacle_placer ship `cycle`, which is declined here as an all-rungs value. So two of the four defaults are the same declined word, one is half of the designed null and would be a poor cell to solve framing on, and one is left. ball is also the pose with the most clearance inside the cage in every direction, which makes it the safest reference cell for a sheet whose figure changes size by a factor of three. reading=body because it is the ONLY reading any of the four members has - all four draw a limb or a row of glyphs and none of them draws an angle or a hull - so `body` is the family's own view and `joints` and `envelope` are this bench's additions. CATEGORY IS COUNTED THE SAME WAY: hazards, because two of the four members live there (armadillo_eggling and spring_hopper in hazards.json) against one in lab.json and one in qfep.json. 2 of 4, counted rather than assumed.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, where each word came from, what KIND of thing its member meant by it, and the six angles each one resolves to.

THE FAMILY FIRST, and it is a census before it is an argument. Four artifacts declare an axis called `posture` and NO TWO OF THEM SHARE A VALUE LIST:

  armadillo_eggling   ball | walker                          default ball        2 values
  spring_hopper       cycle | drawn | laden | solid          default cycle       4 values
  tentacle_placer     cycle | sentry | stoop | coil | cast   default cycle       5 values
  qfep_formula_3d     line | stack | arc | ring              default line        4 values

Fifteen words, four scenes, four scripts, one overlap. Checked: these are four distinct .tscn files on four distinct scripts, not one scene wearing four names.

DOES `cycle` MEAN THE SAME THING IN BOTH MEMBERS THAT USE IT? YES, to the letter, and the check was worth running because it is the only place the family agrees about anything. spring_hopper's header calls it "sentinel: the state machine keeps sole ownership of _compression. Shipped." tentacle_placer's calls it "the shipped ritual ... Wall-clock dependent, exactly as it ships. THE DEFAULT", and its `_is_pinned()` tests `posture != "cycle"` by name. Both mean: DO NOT PIN THIS BODY, hand it back to the clock. Both are their member's shipped default. Both are the un-pinned branch of an is-pinned test. Same meaning, same shape, same role.

WHICH MAKES `cycle` AN ALL-RUNGS VALUE, AND WAVE 20's FIFTH. A still of `cycle` is a sample of the whole axis taken by the shutter - the exact fault the all-rungs rule exists to stop, moved out of space and into time. The two are not equally bad and the difference is measurable rather than argued: spring_hopper's cycle idles at _compression = 0.05 + 0.05 * sin(phase), a bounded neighbourhood of `extended` so narrow that its own header says an "extended" rung "would photograph as a near-duplicate of cycle"; tentacle_placer's cycle runs the entire ritual, rise 7 m, render a cube, descend, place a pyramid, three times, then drift to rest. One is nearly a pose. The other is the union of every pose the artifact can hold. Both are declined and both are in `declines` with their arithmetic.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, and it is the finding. The brief said the four vocabularies are four different KINDS of thing: a defence STATE that an animal switches under threat, a mechanical LOAD that is a number rather than a choice, an animal STANCE, and a typographic LAYOUT with no body in it. Read against the sources that is three quarters right, and the wrong quarter is the interesting one:

  armadillo_eggling's ball/walker IS NOT A BINARY AND IS NOT A SWITCH. `_fold_amount` is a float on [0, 1] and armadillo_droideka._apply_fold_pose(fold) drives EVERY hinge off it linearly - scutes at (scute_open_degrees + fan) * fold, the two equator rings at -+ring_open_degrees * fold, the core at core_raise_height * fold, and each leg at lerp(leg_folded_hip_degrees, leg_deployed_hip_degrees, fold) with the same lerp on the knee. The eggling's own apply_grid_config writes `_fold_amount = 1.0 if posture == "walker" else 0.0`. Two words, one scalar, sampled at its two ends.

  spring_hopper's drawn/laden/solid is THE SAME MECHANISM. `_apply_posture()` writes one float, `_rest`, at -0.25, 0.40 and 0.90, and `_rest` drives the coil's Y-scale, the head height and the head's squash. Two nouns, one scalar, sampled in the middle instead of at the ends.

  SO THE STATE AND THE LOAD ARE ONE VARIABLE WEARING TWO WORDS. `_fold_amount` and `_compression` do the same job by the same means, and the only difference between the two vocabularies is where on the interval each member decided to stand. That is not four kinds of thing; it is THREE. A SCALAR (armadillo_eggling, spring_hopper). A TARGET POINT (tentacle_placer pins a Vector3 and solves a chain to it). An ARRANGEMENT (qfep_formula_3d distributes N items along a path, `_arrange_curved(total_width, sweep)`).

WHAT THIS BENCH IS. One articulated body: a mount, and a chain of SIX equal 0.070 m links on SIX hinges, bending in one vertical plane. A posture is SIX NUMBERS, one angle per hinge in degrees, and nothing else. THERE IS NO ROOT ROTATION, and that is a decision the members force: none of the four axes controls how its artifact is mounted. qfep arranges in its own local frame with x horizontal because a formula is read left to right; tentacle_placer solves in its own with y up because an arm rises from a pedestal. Mount orientation is a property of the artifact, not of the value. Putting four vocabularies on one body means picking one mount, and once you have picked one the words become comparable - which is the whole instrument.

POSTURE, ten values, grouped by member and labelled by kind. Angles are given in hinge order, hinge 0 at the mount.

  ball    STATE  - armadillo_eggling, _fold_amount = 0. The member's own folded angles, hip and knee alternating down the chain exactly as a limb alternates them: -116, +132, -116, +132, -116, +132, from armadillo_droideka.gd's leg_folded_hip_degrees = -116.0 and leg_folded_knee_degrees = 132.0. A packed zigzag that advances only 16 degrees per hip-knee pair. Spans 0.145 x 0.169 m, hull 0.0219 m2, tip 0.166 m from the mount. THE MOST COMPACT BODY IN THE SHEET BY REACH AND NOT BY VOLUME, which is the envelope reading's argument.

  walker  STATE  - armadillo_eggling, _fold_amount = 1. The same two hinges at the other end of the same lerp: +34, -26, +34, -26, +34, -26 (leg_deployed_hip_degrees = 34.0, leg_deployed_knee_degrees = -26.0). Net +8 per pair, so the chain leans out and up with a visible hip-knee wiggle rather than a smooth arc - the alternation is the tell that this vocabulary is anatomical and the other three are not. 0.197 x 0.356 m, hull 0.0247, tip 0.407.

  laden   LOAD   - spring_hopper, _rest = 0.40. Uniform 12.78 degrees per hinge, DERIVED AND NOT CHOSEN: that member scales its coil height by 1 - (1 - _coil_floor) * _compression with the shipped STOCK_COIL_FLOOR = 0.15, so 0.40 leaves 0.66 of full height. A coil gets shorter by compressing; A CHAIN OF RIGID LINKS HAS NO OTHER WAY TO GET SHORTER THAN TO BEND, so the angle is whatever makes the chain's height match the coil's. Bisected on [0, 30] degrees, where the height ratio falls monotonically from 1.000 to -0.167. 0.275 x 0.277 m, hull 0.0350, tip 0.390.

  solid   LOAD   - spring_hopper, _rest = 0.90. Same law, 0.235 of full height, uniform 20.93 degrees per hinge. 0.328 x 0.157 m, hull 0.0402 - THE LARGEST HULL IN THE SHEET, which is the second thing the envelope reading refutes: a spring crushed to its floor occupies more space than one standing free, because a chain that loses height by bending has to put that length somewhere. Tip 0.343.

  sentry  STANCE - tentacle_placer, POSTURE_TARGETS["sentry"] = Vector3(0, 6.0, 0), scaled by this chain's length ratio 0.070 to (0, 0.420). The member's chain is 6.0 m long and its target is at exactly 6.0 m, which its own header notices - "Target 6.0m up = the chain's exact length, so this takes the unreachable branch and stands as a rigid vertical mast" - and the branch's comment reads "Unreachable - straighten the chain at the target." So: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. 0.000 x 0.420 m, hull 0.0135, tip 0.420.

  coil    STANCE - tentacle_placer, target (0, 2.1, 0.4) scaled the same way to (reach 0.028, height 0.147). Distance 0.150 m against a 0.420 m chain, so 36 per cent of reach and therefore a hard curl: -96.40 then 42.87 five times, 257 degrees of total turn. The first link swings almost horizontal and the rest wind back up, ending over the mount - "folded back over its own pedestal ... occupying only itself", which is the member's caption and is what the geometry does. 0.167 x 0.188 m, hull 0.0347, tip 0.150.

  cast    STANCE - tentacle_placer, target (0, 2.4, 5.2) scaled to (reach 0.364, height 0.168). Distance 0.401 m against 0.420, so 95.5 PER CENT OF THE CHAIN'S OWN LENGTH - the longest reach in the sheet, and it is the member's number UNCAPPED. The cage was widened to hold it rather than the reach being capped to fit the cage, and the difference matters: at a cap of 0.855 this value collapses onto `arc` at 3 mm and the closest pair in the sheet becomes an artifact of a rig decision instead of a fact about two vocabularies. Solved 39.76 then 10.19 five times: one hinge aims, five bend alike. 0.364 x 0.169 m, hull 0.0313, tip 0.401.

  line    LAYOUT - qfep_formula_3d, the shipped centring pass, which is _arrange_curved at sweep 0: no turn at any item. [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. IDENTICAL TO `sentry` BY CONSTRUCTION and registered as the designed null. 0.000 x 0.420 m, hull 0.0135, tip 0.420.

  arc     LAYOUT - qfep_formula_3d, `_arrange_curved(total_width, deg_to_rad(110.0))`. The member spreads its terms over 110 degrees of arc; six hinges spread a body over the same 110 degrees at 18.33 each. The member has eleven terms and this bench has six links - THE SWEEP IS WHAT THE VALUE DECLARES and the sweep is what is preserved. 0.324 x 0.183 m, hull 0.0390, tip 0.360.

  ring    LAYOUT - qfep_formula_3d, `_arrange_curved(total_width, TAU)`. 360 degrees over six hinges is 60.00 each, and six links each turning 60 degrees CLOSE: the last link ends exactly at the mount it left, tip distance 0.000 m, the only zero in the sheet. That is what "no vantage shows the whole equation at once" comes to when the thing being arranged is a body. 0.121 x 0.140 m, hull 0.0215 - within 1.9 per cent of `ball`'s 0.0219, which is a coincidence about volume and NOT a null, because the two hulls sit on opposite sides of the mount. Tip 0.000.

SO WHAT DOES THE UNION SHOW? THREE CONSTRUCTIONS, TEN WORDS, AND ONE COLLISION. Read the ten angle vectors and the vocabularies sort themselves without reference to what anyone called them: armadillo alternates two large opposed angles (the anatomical one), spring_hopper and qfep both hand every hinge the same number (the two that are secretly the same construction - a constant curvature, differing only in whether the number is called a compression or a sweep), and tentacle_placer spends hinge 0 aiming and bends the other five alike. `line` and `sentry` are the same six numbers. That is four vocabularies collapsing to three kinds and ten words collapsing to nine bodies, and not one member could have told you, because each of them has only its own word list and its own mount.

READING, three values. Three readings of one pose vector, not three styles - each is a different body built from the same six numbers.

  body      the limb: six tapered links (0.032 m at the root to 0.018 at the tip) and seven collars 1.22 times wider than their links, so a hinge is a thing you can see rather than a corner you infer. THE ONLY READING ANY OF THE FOUR MEMBERS HAS - all four draw a limb or a row of glyphs, none draws an angle or a volume - so this is the family's own view and the other two are this bench's additions.

  joints    the same chain reduced to 0.010 m rods, and at every hinge a solid SECTOR of material spanning that hinge's own angle, all six at one radius of 0.034 m so the six wedges compare directly. The pose stops being a silhouette and becomes six quantities standing up. A hinge at zero draws nothing, so `line` and `sentry` show six absences and `ball` shows six wedges of 116 and 132 degrees, the two largest in the sheet.

  envelope  the limb is not drawn at all; its place is taken by the convex hull of the seven joint centres, grown by the limb's half-width and extruded through its depth - the volume the body occupies, as one solid. THIS READING REFUTES THE OBVIOUS CLAIM ABOUT IT, which was in the brief and is worth stating because it sounds right: a defence state is supposed to minimise the volume occupied, and `ball` does not. Measured on the replica, the hull ladder runs sentry = line 0.0135, ring 0.0215, ball 0.0219, walker 0.0247, cast 0.0313, coil 0.0347, laden 0.0350, arc 0.0390, solid 0.0402. THE SMALLEST HULL IN THE SHEET IS THE STRAIGHT STICK and the largest is the crushed spring. A straight arm occupies almost no volume and is maximally exposed; what a curl minimises is REACH - 0.166 m at ball against 0.420 at line - and reach is not hull. An armadillo is not minimising its convex hull, it is minimising its largest dimension and hiding its soft side, and only one of those three is a volume.

HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP. Rec.709 luminance is written down so the greyscale reading is checkable rather than hoped: plate 0.180, cage 0.309, mount 0.432, rod 0.561, hull 0.720, limb 0.813, sector 0.885. Nothing that must be told apart within one frame sits within 0.10 of anything else, and no pair anywhere in this sheet is separated by hue at constant brightness. If the critic's colour-only rescue fires here it is reporting a fault, not a rescue.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: a shared axis name is not a shared axis, and four artifacts using one word for four constructions have published a vocabulary they never checked. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: a reader can say `posture` is a perfectly good English word that covers a defence state, a spring's load and a page layout, that natural language works exactly this way, and that demanding one construction behind one word is a category error. The answer is that these are not four English speakers, they are four DNA declarations in one registry that a sweep, a gallery and a critic all read as though they named the same thing - and that the collision between `line` and `sentry` is not a matter of usage but of six identical floats, which no dictionary was going to warn anyone about.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: posture=solid against posture=arc, in the body reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
THE CONTEXT IS THE `body` READING AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT, over all 45 posture pairs, EXCLUDING the registered designed null (line against sentry, 0.00 per cent by construction, registered separately below). Mean per-vertex displacement over the seven joint centres, measured on the replica: solid-arc 0.0232 m, solid-cast 0.0317, walker-laden 0.0332, cast-arc 0.0343, laden-arc 0.0511, laden-solid 0.0738, ball-coil 0.0764. So the named pair is the floor by 27 per cent over its nearest rival, and the two runners-up are both LARGER because the limb width saturates the difference: once two links are further apart than the link is wide, extra separation stops adding changed pixels and only moves them.

WHY THAT PAIR AND NOT A CHOSEN ONE. `arc` is qfep_formula_3d's own sweep of 110 degrees divided by six hinges = 18.33 degrees each. `solid` is spring_hopper's own compression of 0.90 under that member's own coil floor of 0.15, which leaves 0.235 of full height, which a six-link chain reaches at 20.93 degrees per hinge. Neither number was picked and neither member has ever heard of the other. They land 2.60 degrees apart at every one of the six hinges.

THE NUMBER. Perpendicular separation between the two chains at the six joint centres, replica-measured: 0.0032, 0.0094, 0.0182, 0.0290, 0.0409, 0.0532 m. Link widths taper 0.032 to 0.018, so the first three links overlap partially and the last three are fully separated. Changed area per link = 2 * min(mean offset, link width) * 0.070 m: 0.000224, 0.000882, 0.001932, 0.003304, 0.002912, 0.002520 = 0.011774 m2, plus about 0.0023 m2 of collar that is not already inside a link sliver, = 0.0141 m2 in the bending plane.

The bending plane is x-y; at capture_config_sweep's standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) the screen basis is x-hat -> (0.8139, 0.1494), y-hat -> (0, 0.9664), z-hat -> (0.5810, 0.2093), so that plane's area projects with Jacobian 0.8139 * 0.9664 = 0.7866. Changed screen area = 0.0141 * 0.7866 = 0.0111 m2. The subject box is the stage, 0.80 x 0.684 x 0.36, projecting to 0.8603 m wide by 0.8558 m tall = 0.7363 m2. So the changed area is 1.51 per cent of the subject box.

The critic crops to the union of the two frames' subject boxes - identical here, because the stage is - neutralises each frame's corner, greys, resizes to 160 x 160 = 25600 px and takes the mean of the hottest 5 per cent = 1280 px. 1.51 per cent of 25600 is 386 changed pixels, FEWER than the 1280-pixel window, so THE WINDOW DOES NOT FILL AND THE NUMBER IS SET BY AREA, NOT BY CONTRAST: 386 hot pixels and 894 cold ones, ratio 0.302. Both arms stand 0.22 to 0.40 m above a plate whose own screen silhouette is only 0.195 m tall, so most of the changed silhouette is against background rather than against the plate; taking the limb at 0.813 against a background near 0.30 gives 0.52 of albedo separation, and applying the lighting-and-tonemap compression the substance_room replica measured at 0.77 gives 40.2 per cent. 0.302 * 40.2 = 12.1. Registered at 12.0.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. The replica has one key, flat shading, no shadows, no AO and no antialiasing, and every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 12.0 ON THE NAMED PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py, because a value the code cannot reach falls back to `ball` and prints identical tiles; (b) _rejects.json, because both exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=30, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 10 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `reading` collapses to [body] alone - which still contains this pair, but deletes both of the readings this bench added and the two thirds of the designed null that test them.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS THE THESIS, not a spare check. qfep_formula_3d's `line` is the shipped centring pass, which is `_arrange_curved` at sweep 0: no turn at any item, so every hinge is 0.000 degrees. tentacle_placer's `sentry` pins POSTURE_TARGETS["sentry"] = Vector3(0, 6.0, 0) against a chain that is exactly 6.0 m long, so the solve takes the unreachable branch whose own comment reads "Unreachable - straighten the chain at the target" - and a straightened chain aimed straight up is also every hinge at 0.000 degrees. The member's header says as much in words: "Target 6.0m up = the chain's exact length, so this takes the unreachable branch and stands as a rigid vertical mast." Verified on the replica: mean per-vertex distance between the two poses is 0.00000 m, all seven joint centres, to the float. So the two frames are the same six links, the same seven collars and the same stage. Predicted 0.00 per cent focus and 0.00 per cent frame. Anything above 0.5 per cent is render noise; anything above 2 per cent means one of the two values is not reaching the code - check _rejects.json before believing any other number in the sheet.

The same identity, tested through a different construction, which is why it is registered separately rather than assumed. The `joints` reading draws a sector at each hinge spanning that hinge's angle; both poses are all zeros, so `_add_sector` returns false six times and the Angles surface is never committed at all. Both frames are the bare rod armature standing vertically. This one also checks that a zero-angle hinge commits NOTHING rather than a degenerate sliver - if these two frames differ, or if either shows a wedge, the sector builder has a floor problem and every angle in the sheet is suspect.

The same identity through the third construction. Both poses hull to the same 0.0135 m2 slab - the smallest envelope in the sheet, a straight stick 0.030 m wide and 0.450 m tall once grown by the limb half-width. The hull is built by monotone chain over 28 points and this pair is the one case where those 28 points are collinear in x before growing, so it is also the degeneracy test for `_hull`: if the envelope reading can publish a frame here at all, it can publish one for any pose. THE CONTRAST THAT MUST HOLD ALONGSIDE ALL THREE: `line` against `solid` in the envelope reading should be among the widest pairs in the sheet, 0.0135 m2 against 0.0402, a factor of three in area. A null that held there too would mean the envelope reading is not reading the pose.

dna.designed_nulls_why: ONE IDENTITY, TESTED THREE WAYS, AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A CHECK ON IT. Exactly one pair in this sheet is identical by construction and it says the thing the bench exists to say: two artifacts that share no vocabulary, no author's intent and no subject matter - a floating TextMesh equation and a robot arm that places pyramids - independently declared a posture value that resolves to the same six floats, and neither could ever have found that out, because each of them has only its own word list and its own mount. THE BRIEF'S OTHER SUGGESTED NULL IS NOT CONSTRUCTIBLE HERE AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED: it proposed that two postures occupying the same hull would be identical in the `envelope` reading however differently the segments sit inside it. Two postures DO very nearly share a hull AREA - `ring` at 0.0215 m2 against `ball` at 0.0219, 1.9 per cent apart - and they are not remotely identical, because the envelope is drawn IN PLACE and those two hulls sit on opposite sides of the mount: ball curls up and to -x, ring closes down and to +x. Equal volume in different places is not a null, and the near-equality of those two numbers is registered here as a coincidence rather than promoted to a claim.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all ten postures in a row (layout=ladder, 0.86 m pitch, about 8.5 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a ten-wide row in the same spec would frame every single cell against eight and a half metres and photograph a 26 mm link as a hair. `layout` is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. NAME COLLISION, DELIBERATELY LEFT AND SAID OUT LOUD: this export is called `layout`, and LAYOUT is also the label this bench gives to qfep_formula_3d's four contributions to the `posture` axis (line, stack, arc, ring). They are unrelated and neither reads the other - `layout` here means how many figures stand on the plate, LAYOUT there means an arrangement of items along a path. No posture value reads this export and this export changes no posture value; the two are kept apart in the code by never appearing in the same function. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no draw here. Every angle is either a member's own constant, a lerp between two of them, or a bisection on a monotone function evaluated 48 times; there is no RandomNumberGenerator, no FastNoiseLite, no NoiseTexture2D, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer and no tween. That matters because THREE OF THE FOUR SOURCES ARE CLOCKS: armadillo_eggling moves _fold_amount under _physics_process at deploy_duration, spring_hopper's whole posture axis exists because `_compression` was owned by a state machine, and tentacle_placer's own header warns that its FABRIK solver "re-solves every physics frame FROM ITS PREVIOUS SOLUTION". All three had to invent a pinning mechanism to be photographable at all - `_pinned`, `_is_pinned()`, an early `_apply_fold_pose(1.0)` in _ready - and two of them kept the un-pinned branch as their default. This bench has nothing to pin because it never moves.
dna.kin: The four sources are the kin and the relation is unusually distant for a synthesis, because this bench shares their WORD and almost none of their values - two of the fifteen are declined outright and the ten that survive come from four incompatible constructions. armadillo_eggling is a 0.74-scale armoured egg whose truth line is that the simplest enemy teaches the most, contact damage being threat reduced to pure proximity - and `ball` and `walker` here are that sentence's hidden premise, which is that the shell opening was never the weapon: the eggling's posture axis exists precisely to show a deployed body that still has no gun. spring_hopper is a coil on legs whose truth line is that F = -kx is life - and `laden` and `solid` are the x, drawn on a body that has no k, which is why they had to be derived through that member's coil-height law rather than copied. tentacle_placer is a six-metre FABRIK arm that places three pyramids and then idles forever, whose own header argues that the idle IS the artifact because a viewer meets the pose and not the ritual - and `sentry`, `coil` and `cast` are three of its four idles, standing next to seven poses it has never met. qfep_formula_3d is the thesis artifact, the whole book compressed to one line of floating TextMesh, whose truth line is that the formula is a lens rather than an equation to solve - and `line`, `arc` and `ring` are its four arrangements minus the one that is not a curvature. A room holding this bench beside any one of the four is saying that member's word back to it in a body it does not have; a room holding it beside all four is the comparison none of them can perform, because each draws its own posture at its own scale on its own mount in its own scene. ON THE VALUE SIDE this is the corpus's WORST shared vocabulary and the exact opposite of cohort_bench's: four members, fifteen words, one overlap, and the one overlap is a sentinel that means "no value".
declines: `cycle`, FROM BOTH MEMBERS THAT DECLARE IT, AND IT IS WAVE 20's FIFTH ALL-RUNGS VALUE. It is a sentinel in both - spring_hopper: "the state machine keeps sole ownership of _compression. Shipped"; tentacle_placer: "the shipped ritual ... Wall-clock dependent, exactly as it ships. THE DEFAULT", with `_is_pinned()` testing `posture != "cycle"` by name - so a still of it is a sample of the whole axis taken by the shutter, which is the all-rungs fault moved from space into time. THE TWO ARE NOT EQUALLY BAD, and the difference is measurable rather than argued: spring_hopper's cycle idles at _compression = 0.05 + 0.05 * sin(phase), a band 0.10 wide against a declared range of -0.25 to 0.90, so it is 8 per cent of the axis and its own header admits an "extended" rung "would photograph as a near-duplicate of cycle"; tentacle_placer's cycle runs the entire ritual - rise to sky_height 7.0, render, descend, place, three times, then drift to rest_target - so it is the union of every pose the artifact can hold, including all four of its own pinned ones. One is nearly a pose. The other is the axis. Both are out.

`drawn`, spring_hopper's -0.25, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE REASON. That value is the spring in TENSION, standing taller than its own rest: the member's coil-height law 1 - (1 - 0.15) * c returns 1.2125 at c = -0.25, i.e. 121 per cent of full height. A CHAIN OF RIGID LINKS HAS A MAXIMUM LENGTH AND IT IS ALREADY ACHIEVED AT ZERO CURVATURE - the height ratio's supremum is exactly 1.000, at every hinge zero, which is `line` and `sentry`. There is no pose above it. The honest alternatives were both refused: bending the chain backward would encode the SIGN of the load as the sign of the curvature, which is not what tension is and would photograph as a mirror image of `laden`; and scaling the links would stop the axis being six angles. So the one negative value in the whole fifteen-word union is unrepresentable on this body, and that is a fact about hinges rather than about spring_hopper. If this bench ever needs it, the body needs a prismatic joint, which is a different artifact.

`stack`, qfep_formula_3d's fourth arrangement, AND THIS IS THE DECLINE THAT CORRECTED THE BRIEF. The brief treated qfep's four values as one thing, a text LAYOUT, and asked whether a body could be posed into it. Three of them can and one cannot, and the split is visible in the member's own code: `line` is the centring pass, `arc` is `_arrange_curved(total_width, deg_to_rad(110.0))` and `ring` is `_arrange_curved(total_width, TAU)` - all three are ONE CONSTRUCTION, a constant turn per item, which is exactly what a chain of equal links does. `_arrange_stack` is not: it translates each term by a fixed row of font_size * 1.5, sets `mesh_instance.rotation = Vector3.ZERO`, and never turns anything. A translation per item BREAKS a chain; there is no hinge angle that moves a link sideways without turning it. So the LAYOUT vocabulary is not one kind of thing either - three curvatures and one translation - and only the curvatures are poses of a body. That is the interesting half of the brief's question, answered against the guess: a body CAN be posed into a text layout, three times out of four, and the fourth is not a layout of the same kind.

`stoop`, tentacle_placer's fourth stance, DECLINED FOR BALANCE AND NOT FOR TRUTH, which is worth separating from the three above. It is perfectly buildable: target (0, 1.1, 2.7) scaled to (0.189, 0.077), 0.204 m from the mount, solved at -25.15 then 37.20 five times. But its bearing from vertical is 67.85 degrees against `cast`'s 65.24 - THE SAME DIRECTION AT 51 PER CENT OF THE REACH - so it adds a rung to a ladder this sheet already has two ends of rather than a kind to the union. The union is built at two values per scalar vocabulary and three per pointed one (2 STATE, 2 LOAD, 3 STANCE, 3 LAYOUT), so a fourth tentacle value would make one member half the sheet. If the sheet is ever rebuilt at twelve values this is the first thing to add.

THE BRIEF'S ARGUMENT, CORRECTED FROM THE CODE, and it is the biggest change. The brief said the four vocabularies are four different KINDS of thing - a defence STATE, a mechanical LOAD, an animal STANCE, a text LAYOUT - and that only three of the four are about a body. Two of those four are the same construction. armadillo_eggling's ball/walker are the two endpoints of `_fold_amount`, a float on [0, 1] that armadillo_droideka._apply_fold_pose drives every hinge off LINEARLY (scutes, both equator rings, the core height, and each leg by lerp between a folded and a deployed angle); spring_hopper's drawn/laden/solid are three samples of `_rest`, a float that drives the coil's Y-scale, the head height and the head squash by the same means. A defence state that is a lerp is not a state, it is a load with a narrative. So `posture` covers THREE constructions, not four: a scalar, a target point and an arrangement - and the fourth thing the brief was counting was a difference in prose.

FABRIK, FOR THE THREE TENTACLE VALUES, AND THE MEMBER'S OWN HEADER IS THE REASON. tentacle_placer hand-rolls FABRIK at 8 iterations with a joint-angle limit, and its own DNA note explains why FABRIK_ITERATIONS could not be an axis: "the solver re-solves every physics frame FROM ITS PREVIOUS SOLUTION, so after a one-second settle even one iteration per frame has accumulated sixty, and every value converges to the same pose." That is a statement that the solver is PATH-DEPENDENT, which makes any still of it a fact about how long the artifact has been running. This bench solves the same targets as a CONSTANT-CURVATURE arm instead - one bend angle shared by hinges 1 to 5, an aim carried by hinge 0, found by bisection on the Dirichlet kernel sin(3t)/sin(t/2), which is monotone from 6 to 0 on [0, 60] degrees and therefore has exactly one root. Deterministic, closed-form up to a bisection, and it hits all three targets to better than a micron on the replica. The cost is honest and is stated: a real FABRIK chain does not distribute its bend evenly, so `coil` and `cast` here are smoother than that member's own arm would be.

A ROOT ROTATION, which would have made `line` horizontal and `sentry` vertical and DELETED THE DESIGNED NULL. It was the tempting build: qfep reads left to right and a tentacle rises from a pedestal, so give each value its own mount angle and the two words stop colliding. It was refused because NONE OF THE FOUR MEMBERS' AXES CONTROLS A MOUNT. qfep arranges in its own local frame, tentacle_placer solves in its own, armadillo folds in its own; mount orientation is a property of the artifact, and adding it to the axis would have meant this bench inventing a seventh number that no member declares - and then reporting, as a finding, a difference it had put there itself.

A SEVENTH LINK, OR AN ODD COUNT. Six is the smallest count that closes a ring at a whole number of degrees per hinge (360 / 6 = 60), which `ring` needs, and it is even, which armadillo's hip-knee alternation needs. Seven links would make `ring` a 6/7 arc that does not close, and five would put `ring` at 72 degrees per hinge with the last link crossing the first. The count is a constraint from two different members at once and there is exactly one number that satisfies both under twelve.

CLASS COLOUR, OR ANY PER-VALUE PALETTE. Every posture is drawn in the same three materials, so no pair anywhere in this sheet is separated by hue - the difference between two cells is always geometry. It would have been easy and it would have been a gauge: the eye would compare two colour codes instead of two bodies, and the whole point of a union axis is that the words have to be told apart by what they DO to a shape.

ANIMATION, AND EVERY RATE, DURATION AND PHASE. Three of the four members ship time-domain exports and all four refused them as axes: deploy_duration and retract_duration, bounce_period and patrol_speed, travel_speed and dwell_seconds and pyramid_lifetime, pulse_speed and glow_intensity. This bench has none to refuse. Everything is built synchronously inside _ready from arithmetic on the members' constants, and that is not a stylistic preference - it is the reason the sheet can be believed at all, given that two of the four members' DEFAULTS are a value that means "hand this body back to the clock".

THE MEMBERS' SCALE. armadillo_eggling is 0.74-scaled with legs of 0.30 and 0.26 m, spring_hopper's coil is 0.50 m tall, tentacle_placer's arm is 6.0 m and qfep_formula_3d's formula is about 2.0 m wide at font_size 0.15. Everything here is rebuilt on a 0.420 m chain with the RATIOS preserved and named - the armadillo's four hinge angles verbatim in degrees, the spring's coil floor of 0.15 and its two compressions verbatim, the tentacle's three targets scaled by the single length ratio 0.070 and by nothing else, qfep's two sweeps verbatim in degrees. Not one absolute length is shared with any source, and every angle is.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=30 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS TWO THIRDS OF THE EXPERIMENT. `posture` is declared first and is never trimmed; `reading` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 10 x 3 sheet renders as 10 x 1 = `body` only, which keeps the pre-registered pair and one third of the designed null but deletes both of the readings this bench added - the wedges that turn a pose into six visible quantities, and the hull ladder that refutes the claim about what a defence state minimises. At --max=20 it renders 10 x 2 = body and joints, which deletes the envelope reading and with it the sheet's only refutation. Only 30 carries the experiment. Note also that the two axes are 10 and 3, so the cross product is not square and any cap between 10 and 29 produces a RAGGED sheet rather than a smaller one.
